newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE TO GET ITS 16TH STOCK.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE TO GET ITS 16TH STOCK.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Wednesday that one more company would join in trading at this week's session, bringing to 16 the number of traded stocks.
Officials hoped for an increase to 26 by the end of 1996.
"Trading in Uztel shares will start on the bourse (on Thursday)," exchange general manager Stere Farmache told a news conference. "We expect more companies to join in soon."
Uztel SA is a state-owned manufacturer of oilfield equipment and spare parts based in the oil town of Ploiesti, 60 km (35 miles) north of Bucharest.

The company has a share capital of 21.056 billion lei, with the State Ownership Fund holding a 70 percent stake. The remaining 30 percent is held by employees and other stockholders, company technical manager Constantin Coman said.
Uztel general manager Ion Dinu said the company had a turnover of 30 billion lei in the first nine months of 1996, compared with 24 billion lei throughout 1995.
Uztel had a nine-month net profit of 4.0 billion lei this year, up from a 1995 post-tax profit of 2.6 billion lei.
Another 20 companies applied for a bourse listing and Farmache said he expected to have 10 trading by year-end.
Brokers say new listings were good news for the lacklustre bourse. "This is a way to boost exchange activity, especially now when we have competition to reckon with," one said.
The bourse has been sluggish in recent months, with turnover from two weekly sessions at around 100 million lei, compared with peaks earlier this year of 1.5 billion.
An over-the-counter trading system, which was launched a month ago and now lists around 200 companies, makes more on a single day of trading than the bourse does in a week. ($=3,559 lei)
